statement: If the claimed necessity means η_Y monic in all of E, faithfulness of L|E′ and RL(E′)⊂E′ do not suffice. They give only E′-relative monicity.
proof_or_counterexample: E has objects Z,Y,T, distinct f,g:Z→Y, unique h:Y→T and k:Z→T with hf=hg=k, and identities. T is terminal. Let L:E→1, R(*)=T, E′={Y,T}. The restricted L is faithful on each hom-set and RL(E′)⊂E′, but η_Y=h is not monic because f≠g.

statement: With the literal component-isomorphism convention Φ₁(A)≃A_core. The free symmetric monoidal category on arbitrary A must allow all component morphisms; the literal statement is correct when A is a groupoid.
proof_or_counterexample: For A=[0→1], the singleton part has no arrow from 0 to 1 although A does. With all component arrows, extension by tensor products and symmetric coherence gives the usual free symmetric monoidal universal property.

statement: If φ:L⊗L′→1 is an inverse pairing and ψ:L′⊗L→1 is determined by φ⊗id_L=id_L⊗ψ with associators, then ψ=ε(L)(φ∘c_{L′,L}). Equality without ε requires trivial self-braiding.
proof_or_counterexample: An odd one-dimensional superline L with odd inverse has φ=1, φ∘c=-1, while the triangle condition gives ψ=1. The scalar correction ε(L)=-1 is necessary. The general formula follows by moving L past L′ and using the two triangle identities.

statement: Finite-colimit closure of a dense C does not imply the displayed cofinality. It holds for a filtered diagram when every C-object is finitely presentable in E.
proof_or_counterexample: Let E=Set and C a small skeleton of countable sets, dense and closed under finite colimits. The filtered sequence Y_n={0,…,n−1} has colimit N∈C, but id_N:N→N does not factor through any Y_n. Thus its comma category against I is empty. Finite presentability supplies factorization and eventual equality, which repair the claim.

statement: The capture argument requires cofinality larger than every indexing size, achieved by a sufficiently large regular cardinal. Cardinal inequality alone is insufficient.
proof_or_counterexample: At π=aleph_omega a countable list of stages aleph_n is unbounded, although omega<π. With regular κ, fewer than κ stages have a common bound; this captures diagrams, natural transformations, inverse arrows and equality witnesses. File02 later explicitly asks for an index set grand devant the bound.

statement: A quotient of term categories can be full and essentially surjective. A left-exact reflector between topoi need not be full. Restriction along a full essentially-surjective ordinary quotient is fully faithful, but its left adjoint is not automatically left exact.
proof_or_counterexample: On C=[0→1] with the covering {0→1}, PSh(C) has diagrams X1→X0 and sheafification is evaluation at0 followed by the constant-arrow embedding. Let P=(1→1), Q=(empty→1). There is no P→Q, while their sheafifications are both terminal and have one map. The finite Hom enumeration is saved.

statement: The inhabited-object theory with all functions is neither a finite-limit theory with pointwise limits nor an ordinary equational theory. The other displayed theories require their own presentations.
proof_or_counterexample: The two maps1⇉2 in nonempty sets have empty equalizer, outside the category. Nonempty sets have no initial object, whereas an equational variety has the free algebra on the empty set. The source cannot use one algebraic characterization for all six quotients.

statement: If ultralocal means fppf-local as in the displayed lifting condition, noetherian test rings do not detect fppf coverings. The correct conservative family must allow nonnoetherian fppf-local rings.
proof_or_counterexample: Schröer Corollary4.5 shows these noetherian rings are exactly algebraically closed fields: p=p² and Nakayama kill the maximal ideal. Spec(F_p)→Spec(F_p[ε]/ε²) lifts every algebraically closed field point but is not an fppf covering sieve: any faithfully flat extension is injective and cannot kill ε. The finite dual-number computation is saved.

statement: In the given ring signature, irreducibility of Spec is not axiomatizable by a coherent first-order theory. This does not by itself decide whether its classifying topos has some different coherent presentation.
proof_or_counterexample: For n≥2 let A_n=k[x,y]/(xy,x^n,y^n), each with one prime ideal. In a nonprincipal ultraproduct, x and y are nonnilpotent because every fixed power survives eventually, yet xy=0. Its nilradical is not prime. First-order coherent axioms are preserved by ultraproducts, so no such axiomatization in this signature exists. Failure of one site to be coherent is not an intrinsic topos invariant.

statement: The geometric internal unit-or-nilpotent condition permits locally varying exponents. It is weaker than demanding every ordinary section ring A(U) be zero-dimensional.
proof_or_counterexample: In E=Set^N let A_n=k[ε]/ε^{n+1}. Each component satisfies the geometric condition, hence the internal ring does. Global sections are the product, and f=(ε_n) is not nilpotent. On any nonzero idempotent component it is never a unit, so no global unit/nilpotent decomposition exists.

statement: The naive limit-of-representables functor Pro(R)→PSh(R) need not be fully faithful. Pro-objects are fully faithfully represented by covariant left-exact functors with the opposite convention, not by this unrestricted presheaf limit.
proof_or_counterexample: For R=FinSet, a profinite set P maps to the presheaf T↦Map(T,underlying P), since finite discrete test sets impose no continuity. The indicator of the all-zero sequence {0,1}^N→{0,1} is a natural transformation of these presheaves but is discontinuous, hence not a pro-morphism.

statement: For n≥2, the full category of rings with exactly n connected components, with all ring homomorphisms, is not a geometric full subtheory. A theory retaining decomposition/torsor data has different morphisms.
proof_or_counterexample: Take A=k^n and repeat the idempotent endomorphism (a1,…,an)↦(a1,…,a1). Each stage has n connected components, while the filtered colimit is its image k and has one. A geometric full subtheory must be closed under these filtered colimits. The finite k example and idempotent-image calculation are saved.

statement: Faithfully flat modules, with all module maps, are not a geometric full subtheory. Faithfully flat unital algebras are a different case.
proof_or_counterexample: The filtered sequence Z --2→ Z --2→… has faithfully flat terms but colimit Z[1/2]. Tensoring the colimit with Z/2 gives0, so it is not faithfully flat. Multiplication by2 is a module map but not a unital Z-algebra map; that distinction is essential.

statement: If the evaluation M⊗Hom_A(M,A)→A is an isomorphism, M is finite locally free of rank1. Monogenicity holds locally, not necessarily globally.
proof_or_counterexample: Write the inverse image of1 under evaluation as a finite sum of tensors m_i⊗phi_i; the values phi_i(m_i) generate the unit ideal. Locally where one is invertible, m_i is unimodular and M splits as A⊕N. The cross term N⊗A lies in the kernel of evaluation, so injectivity forces N=0. This finite open cover proves M finite locally free rank1. The ideal(2,1+sqrt(-5)) has I²=(2) and norm2, but a²+5b²=2 has no integer solution, so it is invertible and nonprincipal. Hom base change is used only after finite projectivity is established.

statement: There is a rank α such that an accessible functor preserves β-presentables for every β sharply larger than α. Arbitrary sufficiently large regular cardinals cannot replace this condition.
proof_or_counterexample: F(X)=X^N on Set preserves aleph1-filtered colimits. For arbitrarily large singular λ with cf(λ)=omega, a set X of sizeλ is λ^+-presentable but |X^N|=λ^omega>λ by König, so F(X) is not λ^+-presentable. The counterexample uses ordinary regular presentability ranks λ^+.

statement: For κ=aleph1 and C=countable sets, Ind_κ(C)=Set. At singular λ>aleph0 of countable cofinality, some λ^+-presentable sets have no κ-directed presentation by C with a cofinal index set of size≤λ. Thus the unqualified Fil^λ equality fails.
proof_or_counterexample: Let |X|=λ. Such a presentation would yield a cofinal family of≤λ countable subsets of X, since countably many representing stages have a common upper bound. Enumerate this family and choose λ_n↑λ with λ_n<λ. Pick x_n outside the union of the firstλ_n members. The countable set{x_n} is contained in no listed member, contradiction. X is λ^+-presentable in Set.

statement: A small dense C in cocomplete locally small E gives a fully faithful nerve with a left adjoint. But C finitely complete and C→E lex does not make C/X filtered; finite colimits preserved in E give that variance. Essential surjectivity of the colimit extension alone is not density.
proof_or_counterexample: Take C={1}→Set: it is lex and dense, but C/2 is discrete with two objects, hence not filtered. For the essential-surjectivity warning, C a discrete set of two copies of1 maps to Set; its colimit extension Set²→Set is coproduct and essentially surjective, while the nerve X↦(X,X) is not full. Density itself follows from the canonical counit criterion.

statement: A small finite-limit sketch has a locally finitely presentable model category. Its finitely presentable objects are closed under finite colimits and retracts; they need not be closed under finite limits. In the manuscript setting with actual designated limits, the representable models generate the finite-colimit closure.
proof_or_counterexample: Take R=k⊕V with V a countably infinite-dimensional square-zero ideal. Multiplication by a nonzero x∈V is an endomorphism R→R between finitely presented modules; its kernel is V, which is not finitely generated because R acts on V through k. Thus the kernel is not finitely presentable. Finite colimits and retracts of finitely presentable objects are finitely presentable by the Hom/filtered-colimit criterion.

statement: The finite-limit dictionary is valid with the adjoint correction C084. For an arbitrary limits-only doctrine, PSh(R) classifies flat functors, not all operation-preserving functors R→Set; essential points recover Kar(R), not R without idempotent completeness.
proof_or_counterexample: For the finite-product theory R=(finite free abelian groups)^op, operation-preserving Set models are all abelian groups. Flat functors are filtered colimits of its representable models, hence filtered colimits of finite free abelian groups and therefore torsion-free by Lazard. Z/2 is a model but not such a point. Separately SGAIV7.6(e) gives the necessary Karoubi completion for essential points.

statement: Faithfulness of a structure-forgetting morphism on all internal model categories does not imply faithfulness of the induced classifying-topos inverse image. The table’s arrow direction and overwritten adjoint notation also require an ink check.
proof_or_counterexample: Forgetting a group structure is faithful in every topos. The corresponding geometric morphism from the group classifier to the object classifier factors through the proper inhabited-object open subtopos, since every group has its unit. The generic object is not forced inhabited (the empty Set model witnesses propriety). Thus the inverse image is not conservative, hence not faithful: a faithful finite-limit/colimit-preserving functor between topoi reflects isomorphisms.

statement: No for the empty doctrine, and no for finite products. Determination on a retract-dense basis is weaker than generation by the prescribed operations. This counterexample does not refute a separately strengthened finite-limit version.
proof_or_counterexample: For no operations, take the Karoubi completion of the one-object monoid {1,e}, e²=e≠1. Its new retract object is not isomorphic to the original object, but a transformation’s component on it is determined by the component on the original object using the retraction. For finite products take R=FinSet^op and S={2}. Since1 is a retract of2, its component is determined; every n is a finite power of1 in R. Yet products of2 in R have even cardinality2m (including0), so1 and3 are outside the product closure.
